subject.title: [Reliability]: Enforce atomic intent→execution flow to prevent orphan pre-action notices

question: Should the reliability guarantee extend the existing lifecycle, session-operation, and terminal-outcome contracts, or should OpenClaw introduce a separately named begin/exec/commit/abort protocol?
rationale: Both shapes affect public gateway and plugin-visible semantics; choosing the permanent source of truth and compatibility plan requires maintainer intent rather than an autonomous implementation decision.

options.title: Extend existing contracts
options.body: Add intent provenance and structured terminal success-or-abort details to the existing canonical lifecycle and terminal-outcome path.

options.title: Add transaction events
options.body: Introduce separate begin/exec/commit/abort events with explicit protocol-version, client, and migration follow-through.

options.title: Keep observability only
options.body: Retain task, audit, liveness, and terminal snapshots without guaranteeing that natural-language announcements correspond to execution.

recommendation.title: Extend existing contracts
recommendation.body: Add intent provenance and structured terminal success-or-abort details to the existing canonical lifecycle and terminal-outcome path.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing discussion already routes this cross-cutting product-contract choice through this reviewer, with substantial adjacent agent and gateway history.
